newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Ceausescu heir flown to Vienna for surgery.
newsitem.headline: Ceausescu heir flown to Vienna for surgery.

text.p: Nicu Ceausescu, the youngest son of Romania's late Stalinist dictator, was flown to Austria on Wednesday for specialised surgery in a last ditch attempt to treat his serious liver disease, Nicu's brother said.
"His (Nicu's) health condition improved a little bit this evening and he was put on a plane for Vienna where he will undergo emergency surgery," Valentin Ceausescu told Reuters.

Nicu, 45, was rushed to the Bucharest university hospital late on Sunday with internal bleeding, the second after a milder one last month, caused by a varicose oesophagus and severe liver cirrhosis, doctors said.
Nicu's critical health condition as well as lack of modern medical equipment had prevented local doctors from performing vital surgery and prepare him for a liver transplant.

"Romania doesn't have the necessary equipment for a liver transplant so we can't solve here the problems in the case of Nicu Ceausescu," Sorin Oprescu, director of the Bucharest university hospital, said.
He said Nicu had been put in the Vienna municipal hospital where doctors were expected to bring his bleeding under control and prepare him for the liver transplant.

Nicu, groomed to be late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's successor, served three years in jail initially over charges linked to ordering the repression of protests in his fiefdom of Sibiu during the December 1989 revolt in which his father and mother were ousted and shot by a firing squad.
The charge was later dropped and only a five-year sentence for illegal gun possession stuck. He was paroled on health grounds in 1992.
